doc: Payload budgets per consumer profile (kemiller2002/limen#19). Each budget is the measured baseline plus 10%, rounded up to a whole KiB; test/bench-size.test.ts fails when a profile exceeds its budget or loads a forbidden module. Raising a budget needs its own work item saying what grew and why; lowering one after an optimization is encouraged.

history.change: Re-baselined every profile after the binding security policy (src/kernel/binding-policy.ts, kemiller2002/limen#18): each profile that loads the kernel grew by about 2.1 KB gzip (6.8 KB raw). kernel-only and kernel-with-handles exceeded their budgets; the rest had not, but are re-baselined by the same rule so every budget keeps 10% headroom over what ships.
Added kernel-with-focus (kemiller2002/limen#23): the focus pack adds 3876 bytes gzip over kernel-only, and only to applications that register it.
Added kernel-with-schedule (kemiller2002/limen#24): the scheduling pack adds 2689 bytes gzip over the kernel, and only to applications that register it.
Added kernel-with-measure (kemiller2002/limen#25): the measurement pack adds 5605 bytes gzip over the kernel, and only to applications that register it.
Added kernel-with-events (kemiller2002/limen#29): the events pack adds 6208 bytes gzip over the kernel, and only to applications that register it.

Added kernel-with-overlay (kemiller2002/limen#49): the overlay pack, with the shared named-target resolver, adds 5614 bytes gzip over the kernel, and only to applications that register it. Earlier kernel-with-* profiles now also forbid dist/capabilities/overlay/.

Added kernel-with-realtime (kemiller2002/limen#26): the realtime pack, with the shared handle table, adds 5841 bytes gzip over the kernel, and only to applications that register it. Earlier kernel-with-* profiles now also forbid dist/capabilities/realtime/.

Added kernel-with-files (kemiller2002/limen#27): the files pack, with the shared handle table and target resolver, adds 6348 bytes gzip over the kernel, and only to applications that register it. Earlier kernel-with-* profiles now also forbid dist/capabilities/files/.

Added kernel-with-store (kemiller2002/limen#28): the IndexedDB store pack adds 9456 bytes gzip over the kernel (its generated codec is the largest part: the transaction and schema contract is the widest yet), and only to applications that register it. Earlier kernel-with-* profiles now also forbid dist/capabilities/store/.

Added kernel-with-adapters (kemiller2002/limen#30): the adapter host pack, with the shared handle table and target resolver, adds 7419 bytes gzip over the kernel, and only to applications that register it; the reference Web Component adapter is a separate module and is not in this profile. Earlier kernel-with-* profiles now also forbid dist/capabilities/adapters/.

Re-baselined every profile after the Core HTTP profile, protocol 1.3 (kemiller2002/limen#47): Core's generated codec gained the new request and outcome types, and the kernel's Http path gained the response representations, header selection and the XSRF binding. Measured on kernel-with-overlay before and after: +1729 bytes gzip (+6640 raw), on every profile that loads the kernel. kernel-only, minimal-consumer, kernel-with-handles, the two host profiles and kernel-with-focus exceeded their budgets; the rest are re-baselined by the same rule so every budget keeps 10% headroom over what ships. The remaining growth since WI-0053 on the older profiles (about 0.9 KB gzip on kernel-only) is protocol 1.2 form-control state, IME handling and boolean attributes, which had stayed within budget.

Added kernel-with-transfer (kemiller2002/limen#47): the transfer profile pack adds 5340 bytes gzip over the kernel, and only to applications that register it. The files pack gained its explicit fileFor accessor (+157 raw bytes, within its budget). Earlier kernel-with-* profiles now also forbid dist/capabilities/transfer/.
Added kernel-with-fallback-host (kemiller2002/limen#50): the optional fatal-fallback host adds 2340 bytes gzip over the kernel, and only to applications that use it.

Added kernel-with-presentation (kemiller2002/limen#34): the resource-hint and view-transition pack adds 4060 bytes gzip over the kernel, and only to applications that register it. Earlier kernel-with-* profiles now also forbid dist/capabilities/presentation/.

Added kernel-with-environment (kemiller2002/limen#35): the environment evidence and formatting pack adds 4979 bytes gzip over the kernel, and only to applications that register it. Earlier kernel-with-* capability profiles now also forbid dist/capabilities/environment/.

profiles.name: minimal-consumer
profiles.doc: What examples/minimal (the copy shipped in the package) loads: the package root. It carries the reference email engine and federation, which a consumer never registers — see docs/27-performance-baseline.md.

profiles.name: kernel-only
profiles.doc: The ./kernel subpath: BrowserKernel and what it needs, nothing else.

profiles.name: kernel-with-handles
profiles.doc: A representative optional set: the kernel plus capability-support's handle table, the library every handle-returning pack imports.

profiles.name: kernel-with-dotnet-host
profiles.doc: The kernel plus the .NET WebAssembly host adapter (F# and C# guests), excluding the .NET runtime itself.

profiles.name: kernel-with-raw-host
profiles.doc: The kernel plus the raw WebAssembly host adapter (Rust guest), excluding the .wasm module.

profiles.name: kernel-with-focus
profiles.doc: The kernel plus the focus, selection and scroll capability pack (./capabilities/focus), as an application that registers it loads them.

profiles.name: kernel-with-schedule
profiles.doc: The kernel plus the scheduling capability pack (./capabilities/schedule), as an application that registers it loads them.

profiles.name: kernel-with-measure
profiles.doc: The kernel plus the measurement and observer capability pack (./capabilities/measure), with the capability-support libraries it imports, as an application that registers it loads them.

profiles.name: kernel-with-events
profiles.doc: The kernel plus the rich browser event facts capability pack (./capabilities/events), as an application that registers it loads them.

profiles.name: kernel-with-overlay
profiles.doc: The kernel plus the overlay and top-layer capability pack (./capabilities/overlay), with the capability-support target resolver it imports, as an application that registers it loads them.

profiles.name: kernel-with-realtime
profiles.doc: The kernel plus the realtime and streaming capability pack (./capabilities/realtime), with the capability-support handle table it imports, as an application that registers it loads them.

profiles.name: kernel-with-files
profiles.doc: The kernel plus the user-mediated file capability pack (./capabilities/files), with the capability-support libraries it imports, as an application that registers it loads them.

profiles.name: kernel-with-store
profiles.doc: The kernel plus the IndexedDB structured-storage capability pack (./capabilities/store), as an application that registers it loads them.

profiles.name: kernel-with-adapters
profiles.doc: The kernel plus the governed adapter host pack (./capabilities/adapters), with the capability-support libraries it imports, as an application that registers it loads them. Adapters themselves, including the reference Web Component adapter, load separately.

profiles.name: kernel-with-transfer
profiles.doc: The kernel plus the HTTP transfer profile pack (./capabilities/transfer), as an application that registers it loads them. Uploading picked files also loads the files pack, which has its own profile.

profiles.name: kernel-with-fallback-host
profiles.doc: The kernel plus the optional fatal-fallback host (./hosts/fallback), as a composition root that uses it loads them.

profiles.name: kernel-with-presentation
profiles.doc: The kernel plus the resource-hint and view-transition capability pack (./capabilities/presentation), as an application that registers it loads them.

profiles.name: kernel-with-environment
profiles.doc: The kernel plus the environment evidence and formatting capability pack (./capabilities/environment), as an application that registers it loads them.
